items.title: Privileged representational axes in biological and artificial neural networks
items.author: Nancy Kanwisher
items.content: Khosla et al. show that both brains and neural networks consistently favoured certain axes for representing the natural world.

items.title: Refining a new movement by practicing it upside down
items.content: In this study, participants improved at copying an unfamiliar alphabet character even though they only practiced writing rotated versions of it. The experiments reveal that the motor system can refine movements by creating an abstraction of their structure, and not only by repeating the same mechanical muscle commands.

items.title: Trait judgements of faces using a task without word labels
items.author: Ralph Adolphs
items.content: Xu et al. examine how people perceive faces as being associated with psychological traits, using a task that imposes no a priori labels.

items.title: Motor abstraction training generalizes to the refinement of specific movement patterns
items.author: Samuel D. McDougle
items.content: Practicing unfamiliar characters in rotated orientations improved upright writing as much as direct practice, showing that the motor system learns by abstracting a movement’s structure, not just its details.

items.title: The case for AI degrowth
items.author: Steffen Lange
items.content: Artificial intelligence (AI), as it currently unfolds, is incompatible with a sustainable transformation of the economy, which arguably requires degrowth. AI is the growth paradigm reborn — built on enclosed commons, powered by fossil energy, and driven by a competitive logic that makes precaution structurally impossible. Limits to AI growth are not technophobia; they are our best chance for a liveable future for all.

items.title: Petition style changes with AI writing support but outcomes do not improve
items.content: In 2023, Change.org introduced an artificial intelligence (AI)-supported petition-drafting tool to their platform. With access to this tool, users’ petitions changed substantially, and their texts became more similar to one another. At the same time, overall petition outcomes did not improve, which shows the limits of AI integration into online advocacy communities.

items.title: Responsibilism and culture
items.author: Amiryah N. Toves
items.content: Previous research has widely associated East Asian cultures with higher levels of collectivism, which is often measured through self-report scales that emphasize warmth and prosociality towards all people. Talhelm et al. developed a responsibilism scale that captures duties and responsibilities in close relationships.
